items.q: Match the following diabetes association — 1) Haemochromatosis 2) Cushing 3) Acromegaly 4) Pheochromocytoma … A) Bronze diabetes from iron deposition B) Hypercortisolism-induced IR C) Excess GH-induced IR D) Catecholamine-induced hyperglycaemia
items.exp: Haemochromatosis causes bronze diabetes from iron deposition; Cushing produces hypercortisolism-induced insulin resistance; acromegaly causes GH-induced IR; pheochromocytoma causes catecholamine-induced hyperglycaemia. (Book p926)

items.q: A 50-year-old with hypertension, centripetal obesity and purple striae has new diabetes. The most likely diagnosis is:
items.exp: Centripetal obesity, hypertension and purple striae suggest Cushing syndrome as the secondary cause of diabetes. (Book p926)

items.q: Assess acromegaly: I Diabetes improves with treatment of GH excess. II Diabetes persists despite cure of acromegaly in most patients.
items.exp: Diabetes improves with control of GH excess in many acromegaly patients; in some, diabetes persists despite cure. (Book p926)

items.q: Which is the odd one out — a non-pancreatic endocrine cause of diabetes?
items.exp: Insulinoma is a pancreatic tumour that causes hypoglycaemia, not hyperglycaemia; the others cause hyperglycaemia. (Book p926)

items.q: Bronze skin, hepatomegaly and new-onset diabetes suggest ___.
items.exp: Bronze skin with hepatomegaly and diabetes fits hereditary haemochromatosis; iron studies confirm. (Book p926)

items.q: Match the following diagnostic clue to the cause — 1) Elevated transferrin saturation 2) Elevated urinary free cortisol 3) Elevated IGF-1 4) Elevated plasma metanephrines … A) Haemochromatosis B) Cushing syndrome C) Acromegaly D) Pheochromocytoma
items.exp: Transferrin saturation supports haemochromatosis; urinary free cortisol supports Cushing; IGF-1 supports acromegaly; plasma metanephrines support pheochromocytoma. (Book p926)

items.q: A patient on protease inhibitors has new diabetes. The mechanism is most consistent with:
items.exp: Protease inhibitors cause insulin resistance rather than autoimmune destruction. (Book p926)

items.q: Assess post-transplant diabetes: I It is associated with worse graft outcomes. II Tacrolimus has a lower diabetogenic potential than ciclosporin.
items.exp: Post-transplant diabetes worsens graft outcomes; tacrolimus is more diabetogenic than ciclosporin. (Book p926)

items.q: Match the following endocrine tumour to its metabolic effect — 1) Glucagonoma 2) Somatostatinoma 3) VIPoma 4) Insulinoma … A) Necrolytic migratory erythema + diabetes B) Inhibits insulin secretion C) WDHA syndrome D) Hypoglycaemia
items.exp: Glucagonoma causes necrolytic migratory erythema with diabetes; somatostatinoma inhibits insulin; VIPoma causes WDHA; insulinoma causes hypoglycaemia. (Book p926)

items.q: A patient with weight loss, necrolytic migratory erythema and diabetes most likely has:
items.exp: Necrolytic migratory erythema with diabetes is the textbook glucagonoma presentation. (Book p926)

items.q: The classic triad of pancreatic cholera is watery diarrhoea, hypokalaemia and ___.
items.exp: VIPoma causes WDHA: watery diarrhoea, hypokalaemia and achlorhydria. (Book p926)

items.q: Assess these endocrine syndromes: I Acromegaly with diabetes is an indication for IGF-1 measurement. II Pheochromocytoma always presents with sustained hypertension.
items.exp: Acromegaly diagnosis requires elevated IGF-1; pheochromocytoma typically presents with paroxysmal, not always sustained, hypertension. (Book p926)
